::: {#def-plateau}
#### Plateau

Let $f : \reals^p \to \reals$ be a [function](functions.qmd#def-function)
with a [gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative)
at every point of a region,
and let $\epsilon > 0$ be a tolerance.
The region is a **plateau** of $f$ if the
[Euclidean norm](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-euclidean-norm)
of the gradient satisfies

$$
0 < \norm{\deriv{\vx} f(\vx)} < \epsilon
$$

at every point $\vx$ of the region.
The function is then nearly flat on the region,
and the region contains no [stationary point](#def-stationary-point).

:::
